# PR #2921: Patch: watch a friend's Duos game like a 1v1 game

Closes #2881

## Watch a friend's Duos game like a 1v1 game (#2881)

A friend can now watch a live co-op game from their friend's human seat, the same way a 1v1 game is watched (R1107000, R1103000, R2609000, R2615000):
- friends only, at most `SPECTATORS_PER_MATCH` watchers per game;
- each view arrives `SPECTATE_DELAY_MS` late, with `legal: []`;
- nothing a watcher sends reaches the game;
- both human seats are told the watcher count;
- the watch socket closes with 1000 after the view that shows the result.

A stranger, a blocked pair, a full game and the friend's own teammate are refused. An unfriend, a block or the watcher deleting their account drops a watch already running. A watcher only ever gets the friend's seat's `duos_view_for` view plus its clock. It never gets a ping, a `clock` or `teammate` frame, `jloreCapped` or `economy`, and so nothing of the AI team's hidden cards.

New ruling **R2881000** lifts the co-op exclusion in §9.5 and §13. Its §11 paragraph is in `spec/pending/2881.md`. It also edits §9.5, §9.8, §13 (intro, §13.6, §13.9, §13.10) and R2615000's co-op clause.

### What changed
- **Server**
  - `/ws/watch` takes a co-op game's id as well as a 1v1 match's. `social::watch::may_watch` now answers `Option<Watched>`: it checks the `matches` row first, then `duos_matches` (live, friend in a1 or a2, viewer in neither).
  - `DuosActor` gains a watcher section like the 1v1 one, with one recorded view per human seat, and `seat_view` is split out of `push_view`.
  - `DuosRegistry` gains `attach_watcher`, `watcher_count` and `revoke_watchers`. Its reaper keeps a finished actor until every watcher has had the result.
  - Revokes on unfriend, block or account deletion now reach co-op watchers too, through `revoke` and `revoke_watcher`.
  - `GET /api/friends` marks a co-op friend's game `watchable`, unless the viewer is that friend's teammate, and adds `duos: true`.
- **Web**
  - The Watch link carries `&coop=1` for a co-op friend.
  - `WatchRoute` draws a co-op watch on `DuosBoard`, read-only, the way the co-op replay does.
  - The Duos socket reads the `watchers` frame, and `DuosRoute`'s status line shows the count.
- **Docs:** the server README, `docs/architecture.md` §5.4 and the web README.
- **Pass 3 flake fix (outside the plan):** `src/routes/gate.test.tsx` failed now and then. In `net/gate.ts`, `useAccount` saved the gate's answer in a passive effect, which could run after `announceAccountChange()` and put back the answer it had just cleared. That effect is now `useLayoutEffect`, and a new R2630000 test, which fails without the fix, pins it.

### How it was tested
After merging `main`, I re-ran every harness check:
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo jackioh spec check`: "1652 rulings, 3956 proofs, 48926 citations in 3178 files, 21151 links: ok".

- `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh`, then the harness's `vitest run --project web --changed origin/main …`: 214 files, 4228 tests passed.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and `pnpm exec eslint apps/edge apps/web e2e`: clean.
- `jackioh classify --base f887a784 --claims`: "App", so no card plays differently and no patch fragment is owed.

**Flaky cargo test.** The journal shows `cargo tests` failing on two of the harness's check runs and passing on the next run each time, with no Rust change in between. To check whether this branch's tests are the cause:
- I ran the 9 `r2881000` server tests 25 times in a row and 72 more times with 12 copies at once on 4 cores. None failed.
- The whole server test binary passed: 1682 tests.

So nothing points to this branch. I couldn't see the failing runs' logs, so I can't name the test that failed there.

### Decisions the issue did not settle (alternatives rejected)
- **Same socket:** co-op watching uses `/ws/watch` and its hello, and the server tells the two kinds apart by the match id. I rejected a second `/ws/duos-watch` path, which would duplicate the sign-in, the hello and the refusals.
- **Same route:** the web link adds `&coop=1` to the existing `/watch/:matchId` instead of adding a new route.
- **New ruling:** the change reverses spec text and R2615000's own wording, so it gets its own ruling rather than a quiet edit.
- **Whole seat view:** a watcher sees the seat's full §13.6 view, including the teammate's duel, not just the friend's own duel, so the board matches what the seat itself is shown.
- **Teammate refused:** the friend's own teammate already holds a seat in the game, so they are refused, as a 1v1 player watching their own match is.
- **Reaper waits:** a finished actor is kept until each watcher has had the result view, at most `SPECTATE_DELAY_MS` longer. Otherwise the sweep would drop it as soon as both people left.
- **Fold on demand:** a watch of a game not in memory folds the actor back, so a server restart does not refuse every co-op watch until the sweep reloads the game.

### A person must decide
**The Privacy Policy wording is left unchanged.** `routes/privacy.tsx` says your friends and your opponent's friends may watch your games. After this change, your co-op teammate's friends also see your duel as your teammate sees it, your hand included. Changing that wording moves `PRIVACY_LAST_UPDATED` and with it `TERMS_VERSION`, so every account would have to accept the terms again (R970001). The page is also marked as needing owner and legal review, so a person should decide whether and how to reword it.

### Worth a second look
- `crates/server/src/duos/actor.rs`, the "Watchers" section: every watcher socket is closed only after the actor's lock is dropped, because a socket's close handler takes the lock again.
- `social/presence.rs`: the viewer's own id is added to the `presence_in_duos` read, so a teammate is never shown their own game as watchable.

# #2881: Patch: watch a friend's Duos game like a 1v1 game
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Today you can watch a friend's live 1v1 match from their side, a few seconds behind. You cannot watch a friend's co-op game at all. After this change, watching works for co-op too: you see your friend's team view on the same delay, and the game plays on exactly as before.

## Why

- The spec explicitly excludes co-op from watching (`spec/09-architecture.md` §9.5: "A co-op game cannot be watched (§13)"), while all the machinery watching needs already exists for Duos: `duos_view_for`, the co-op board (`apps/web/src/duos/DuosBoard.tsx`), and the friend/presence/challenge plumbing.
- Co-op is the social mode (§13, `/together`); not being able to spectate it is the gap players will notice first, and pings already being teammate-only and unlogged (B39, `crates/server/src/duos/actor.rs`) shows the design knows how to keep watchers out of the game.
- This is new: issue #2739 is about watching an opponent Discover in 1v1 (different feature), and no rejected suggestion covers spectating.

## Proposal

- Mirror the 1v1 watch contract for one co-op seat: friend-only, at most `SPECTATORS_PER_MATCH` watchers, each view `SPECTATE_DELAY_MS` behind, no legal actions, watcher frames never reach the reducer, count changes announced, socket closed once the result view is sent (R1107000, R1103000, R2615000).
- The watcher sees the friend's seat view (own plus what the team shares, §13.6), never the AI team's hidden state and never pings; a finished co-op game stays replay-only via the existing co-op replay file (R1242000).
- Spec change: lift the §9.5 exclusion with a short paragraph naming the delay, the cap and whose view a watcher gets.

## Where it lands

- `spec/09-architecture.md` §9.5 and §13 (the exclusion and the watch contract); `crates/server/src/duos/` (watch socket beside `actor.rs`); `apps/web/src/duos/` (watch route on `DuosBoard.tsx`); engine `duos_view_for` reused, not changed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A friend can watch a live co-op game from the friend's seat view, delayed, with no actions offered and nothing they do affecting the game.
- [ ] A non-friend, a full game, and a blocked pair are refused exactly like 1v1 watch; ending the friendship or blocking mid-watch drops the watcher.
- [ ] Watch count changes reach both human seats; the socket closes after the result view.
- [ ] The AI team's hidden hands/decks are unreachable from watch traffic (a test holds a watcher to the friend's `duos_view_for` bytes).

## Size and risks

Medium-large: server plus client plus spec; `difficulty:hard` (design across crates). Main risk is leaking hidden co-op state through a new socket; mitigate by sending only already-filtered `duos_view_for` frames, as 1v1 watch does with `view_for`.
